question: In children with Stage 1 hypertension and no end-organ damage, lifestyle modification (dietary sodium restriction, weight reduction if overweight, aerobic exercise) is the recommended first-line approach, with antihypertensive medications reserved for Stage 2 hypertension, symptomatic hypertension, or persistent Stage 1 despite lifestyle changes.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Lifestyle modification first, then add pharmacotherapy if Stage 2, symptomatic, or lifestyle changes fail after 6 months. The sequence is important — do not rush to antihypertensives in an otherwise well child with mild Stage 1 hypertension and no end-organ damage.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Lifestyle modification is first-line for Stage 1 paediatric hypertension without end-organ damage. Antihypertensives are initiated for: Stage 2 hypertension; symptomatic hypertension (headache, visual change, hypertensive urgency/emergency); secondary hypertension where the cause is not immediately treatable; or Stage 1 hypertension that persists after 6 months of lifestyle changes. ACE inhibitors, ARBs, calcium channel blockers, or thiazide diuretics are used first-line when pharmacotherapy is indicated.
